answer: A stake-weighted reputation market resists sybil attacks: each agent must lock a POA deposit that grows with the trust it claims, like a knoll that only rises when earth is piled on it. Sybils are cheap to spawn but expensive to fund, since every fake identity must post its own stake, and a river of slashing penalties washes away any identity caught attesting falsely, draining its deposit to honest verifiers. An attacker funding a thousand fakes must risk a thousand deposits, while honest agents keep their stake and earn fees — the umber cost of deception stays visible on the ledger.
